candidate_evidence.quote: Salovum®, a product based on the egg yolk powder B221®, contains high levels of AF and is classified as a "food for special medical purposes" by the European Food Safety Agency.
Since Salovum® is not classified as a drug, clinical trials have only required ethics approval.
[DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT] Salovum (other names: Antisecretory factor): Ingestion of Salovum 11g three times daily during 48 hours

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: in participants undergoing diagnostic biopsies for suspected glioblastoma

role_evidence.quote: Since Salovum® is not classified as a drug, clinical trials have only required ethics approval.

agents.drug_class_hint: egg yolk powder enriched in antisecretory factor; food for special medical purposes (not a licensed medicine)
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: lower interstitial fluid pressure and enhance the efficacy of both systemic and intratumoral temozolomide treatment

coder_notes: Salovum is a dietary supplement / food for special medical purposes, explicitly 'not classified as a drug', so excluded intervention type (supplement without marketing authorisation). Single-arm sequential pre/post design in patients undergoing diagnostic biopsy for suspected glioblastoma; treatment setting coded newly_diagnosed. Pharmacodynamic intratumoral measurements are planned for Salovum (intratumoral pressure, pO2, cytokines in microdialysate) but Salovum is not a candidate, so tumour_pk_planned and target_engagement_planned coded no; cytokines are not listed as tumour molecular biomarker rows.
